memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I will set my face against anyone who turns to mediums and spiritists to prostitute themselves by following them, and I will cut them off from their people. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the LORD your God. Keep my decrees and follow them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.'" - Lev 20:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two commands sit side by side in these verses, and at first they seem to contradict each other.

Consecrate yourselves and be holy. That sounds like our work.

I am the LORD, who makes you holy. That is clearly His work.

Both are true, and holding them together is the heart of the Christian life. God makes us holy — it is His doing, His initiative, His power. And we are called to pursue holiness actively, not passively wait for it to happen to us.

Paul puts both in one breath: continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfil his good purpose (Phil 2:12-13). Work out — because God works in.

Get this wrong in one direction and you get exhausting self-effort, trying to manufacture change by willpower. Get it wrong the other way and you get passivity, waiting for God to zap you while nothing changes.

The truth is better than both. You genuinely strive, and the striving itself is God's work in you.

I am the LORD, who makes you holy. That is a promise you can build a life on.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend towards self-effort or towards passivity?
2. What does it mean that God is the one who makes you holy?
3. Where do you need to actively pursue what God is already working in you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are the one who makes me holy. Work in me, and let me pursue You actively, knowing the strength for it comes from You. Amen.
